title: CXLfork: Fast Remote Fork over CXL Fabrics
problem: Remote process cloning across cluster nodes incurs high serialization and copying overhead, creating large cold-start latency for serverless functions and other scale-out workloads. Traditional fork() semantics do not map efficiently to distributed shared memory environments like CXL-attached memory.
motivation: CXL interconnects enable globally-shared memory pools across nodes, and exploiting this for process cloning can eliminate cold-start bottlenecks in serverless computing without the overhead of network-based state transfer.
method: CXLfork implements a remote fork interface (a way to copy a running process to a different computer in a cluster) using CXL-attached shared memory—specialized memory physically connected to multiple machines that can all access it directly. Instead of copying the process's pages and metadata over the network, it stores everything in this globally-shared CXL memory, so if multiple processes need the same data, it only exists once instead of being duplicated. The system smartly splits storage between fast local DRAM and the slower shared CXL memory: pages that are frequently used stay in local DRAM for speed, while pages that are rarely used or shared across processes live in CXL memory. CXL-porter builds on this to efficiently scale serverless functions (small on-demand tasks) by spawning multiple copies of a function across cluster nodes without the network copying overhead.
key_novelty: Using CXL-attached globally-shared memory for cluster-wide deduplication of process state, so remote process cloning runs nearly as fast as local cloning.
contributions: CXLfork: a remote fork interface achieving close to zero-serialization, zero-copy process cloning over CXL fabrics
Cluster-wide process-state deduplication using CXL shared memory
Fine-grained state tiering between local DRAM and CXL memory
CXL-porter: an efficient horizontal autoscaler for serverless functions built on CXLfork

metrics.speedup: 2.26x over state-of-practice restore latency on average
metrics.other: 87% reduction in local memory consumption on average

baselines: state-of-practice remote fork / serverless cold-start mechanisms
limitations: Results depend on CXL fabric availability; performance on real CXL hardware vs simulation is not detailed in the abstract.
primary_theme: CXL-enabled zero-copy remote process cloning for serverless scale-out
